audit.why: Full phases[].side, content win[] and packet.levelChart all read Akali on all seven rows. That matches the kit — Ziggs has no dash, no self-peel beyond one knockback, and nothing that fights at 350 range. No chart edit proposed. One prose misalignment was fixed: whys[1] sits on the Level 2 row but described 'levels 3-5'.
audit.corrected: whys[1] rewritten to describe level 2, the row it actually renders on.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[3].why and phases[5].why were generic Akali boilerplate carrying no Ziggs content, and no field anywhere gave a cooldown.
audit.why: Satchel Charge is 20/18/16/14/12s and Hexplosive Minefield is a flat 16s at every rank — the flat 16 is unusual and worth knowing, because unlike most zoning tools it never gets shorter.
audit.corrected: Both phases regrounded with the real numbers and the abilities that own those stages.

audit.whatIsWrong: Hexplosive Minefield (E) was not mentioned anywhere on the page — not once, in either layer. Short Fuse's empowered auto was also absent. Meanwhile Satchel Charge was called 'short-ranged'.
audit.why: The minefield is the actual anti-approach tool in this matchup: 900 range, a flat 16s, proximity mines that slow on contact. Akali's entire game plan is closing 350 range, and the thing that stops her is the mines, not the knockback. Telling her to watch only the satchel points her at the wrong button. Short Fuse periodically empowers his next auto and its cooldown drops every time he casts, so his wind-up — not his ability cast — is the cue to step back. And Satchel Charge is 1000 range, not short-ranged.
audit.corrected: Hexplosive Minefield now named in breakdown.cooldowns, enemyWin, phases[3].why and spikes[0]; the Short Fuse auto tell written into wants.foe[3]; the satchel's real 1000 range implied by fixing the 'short-ranged' claim to a cooldown-based punish.

audit.why: The missingInteractions file carries a 'resistances-invalidated' rule for Satchel Charge, which would normally mean 'do not stack raw armour or MR'. I did NOT write it. Riot's own text for Satchel Charge is a knockback that damages enemies and lets Ziggs hexplode vulnerable TURRETS — there is no percent-health component against champions. The derived percentHealth flag has misfired on the turret clause, exactly the tooltip-parsing failure mode the brief warns about, so per the rule I trusted the description.

audit.whatIsWrong: enemyWin and breakdown.carry were structural templates.
audit.why: 'wins by landing X, denying your pattern' and 'Carry through deletions' paste onto any enemy.
audit.corrected: Both regrounded on the minefield, the satchel and his poke range.

edits.before: - Ziggs Satchel Charge: matchup-defining — His knockback escape — he is catchable only while it is down. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your W Twilight Shroud like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Satchel Charge: 20s at rank 1, 12s maxed — the knockback is his only escape, so he is catchable every second it is down. - Hexplosive Minefield is a flat 16s at every rank and slows on contact: the mines stop your approach, not the bomb.

edits.before: Ziggs wins by landing Satchel Charge, denying your pattern, and renting you the lane at a range markup.
edits.after: Ziggs wins by mining your approach with Hexplosive Minefield, satcheling himself clear, and poking from 850 all game.

edits.before: Carry through deletions — one carry per fight, every fight; the shroud buys the time and the resets pay the exit.
edits.after: Ziggs is the deletion and he knows it — walk around the minefield, wait out the satchel, then R in. He has nothing else.

edits.before: Passive-weave every trade: spell, walk out of the ring, auto the edge — the energy refunds pay the whole lane.
edits.after: Hexplosive Minefield slows on contact on a flat 16 seconds — path around the mines and he has no second answer.

edits.before: First item spike: shroud trades become kill threats. Force the wave contact and punish every spell he whiffs.
edits.after: Your first item closes his 850 in one flip — punish every Bouncing Bomb he spends on the wave instead of you.

edits.before: His Q poke is dodgeable and he has no all-in tools once you're in range, keeping levels 3-5 firmly in your favor.
edits.after: His Bouncing Bomb is dodgeable and he has no all-in tool once you are inside 350, so level 2 stays firmly yours.

edits.before: Ziggs' Bouncing Bomb (Q) poke pattern is strong on paper but has a long cast animation you can dodge with E flip repositioning, and once you're in his face his mobility is nonexistent — punish any missed Q with an immediate all-in.
edits.after: Ziggs' Bouncing Bomb (Q) looks strong on paper but the arc is dodgeable with an E flip, and once you are in his face his mobility is nonexistent — the real gate is Hexplosive Minefield, so path around the mines and punish any missed Q.

edits.before: Punish his short-ranged W (Satchel Charge) cooldown — he can't kite you twice in a row
edits.after: Punish the 20-second Satchel Charge window — he cannot knock you away twice in a row

edits.before: Siege turrets and objectives with W-passive damage rather than fighting you directly
edits.after: Hexplode vulnerable turrets with Satchel Charge instead of ever fighting you directly

edits.before: Zone with Q wave-clear range to deny your CS and roam timers
edits.after: Chip you with the Short Fuse empowered auto every time he casts

notes: Biggest gap: Hexplosive Minefield appeared nowhere on this page, in either layer. It is the ability that actually denies Akali's approach — 900 range, flat 16s at every rank, proximity mines that slow on contact — while the page pointed the player exclusively at Satchel Charge. Now named in four fields. Satchel Charge was also described as 'short-ranged'; it is 1000. Short Fuse's empowered auto (the auto-reset tell from missingInteractions) added to wants.foe[3]. DELIBERATELY NOT WRITTEN: the missingInteractions file carries a 'resistances-invalidated' rule for Satchel Charge, but Riot's text shows no percent-health damage against champions — the percentHealth flag has misfired on the clause about hexploding vulnerable TURRETS. Writing 'armour is the wrong answer here' off a turret mechanic would be a fabricated itemization rule, so I left it out. The packet suspectName 'Use Satchel Charge' is a FALSE POSITIVE. Chart needed no work; I did fix whys[1], which sat on the Level 2 row while describing levels 3-5. Unverified and therefore left alone: whether Satchel Charge's knockback can interrupt Akali's E dash or R recast mid-flight, whether mines detonate on a shrouded (untargetable) Akali, and whether Twilight Shroud blocks Mega Inferno Bomb's damage. This matchup also confirms the brief's warning about packet.games — MC_REAL_GAMES reports 2013 games here and the matchup was audited on that basis.
